object_description: two buildings arranged around an orthogonal crossroads, a five-storey school and a sports volume
geometry_property: two-storey plinth band with high supports
design_condition: all uses are arranged around an orthogonal crossroads, with the school in the southern quadrant, the sports building in the northern, and the playing field and playground in the two remaining quadrants

positive: All uses are arranged around an orthogonal crossroads with a clear quadrant logic
The school building accommodates the arrival situation of the neighbouring care centre
Both buildings have a clear static structure visible in the high-quality facade
The light brick cladding creates a reference to the former neighbouring industrial area
A two-storey plinth band with high supports surrounds the buildings and encloses the arcades of the crossroads
These arcades serve as a break hall
The folded facade relief of the classroom storeys offers advantages for summer thermal protection
The clever positioning allows a spacious open green area with a sensible division into school and public space
Park continuity, terrain modelling and tree placement create harmonious connections and differentiated zoning
Changing areas allow a variety of visual references experienced through the pathways
The entrance with playground and public uses is connected to the park with overlapping tree groups
A legible zoning is created with the seating wall
Playground and school garden are sensibly positioned
A place of retreat with quality of stay is created between sports hall and park
The central entrance hall and spacious staircase give access to three compact upper floors
Six well-functioning clusters are created on three floors
The stairwell is lit centrally and naturally from the side by the common rooms
The hall on the lower basement level is naturally lit
The proposed materialisation is assessed as very solid and durable
The project impresses with its clarity and unambiguousness at a superordinate urban planning level
negative: The rather high mounds with the necessary earth fillings are inappropriate and obstruct the open spaces
The swimming pool is accessible only via a complicated route
The awkward arrangement of the checkrooms in the basement is not obvious
The all-weather pitch on the roof does not meet the requirements for the desired field dimensions
The volumetric division results in a relatively large facade area and a deficit in compactness
The materialisation is expensive to construct
The complex layout of the sports building would need to be revised
Important functional concerns are not at the level of the design issues
